locklog doctor: what the agent's account can reach here (advisory: a check, not a boundary)

  RED   the Docker engine answers the agent's account (DOCKER_HOST is set): it can start a container that reads every log and the console's volumes
        remedy: run the agent where the Docker socket and DOCKER_HOST are out of reach (not in the docker group, no socket mounted), or in a container of its own (locklog setup --agent container)
  RED   group docker: the agent's account is a member; the docker group is root on this host: it starts a container that reads every log
        remedy: take the agent's account out of the docker group (sudo gpasswd -d $USER docker), or run the agent in a container of its own (locklog setup --agent container)
  RED   group adm: the agent's account is a member; the adm group reads /var/log
        remedy: take the agent's account out of adm (sudo gpasswd -d $USER adm): the console reads the logs for it
  RED   group systemd-journal: the agent's account is a member; the systemd-journal group reads the whole journal
        remedy: take the agent's account out of systemd-journal (sudo gpasswd -d $USER systemd-journal)
  RED   sudo -n true succeeds: the agent can become root without a password
        remedy: remove the NOPASSWD rule (or the sudo timestamp) of the agent's account, or run the agent in an account without sudo
  RED   euid 0: the agent runs as root, which reads everything the console guards
        remedy: run the agent in an unprivileged account
  RED   /var/log/journal is readable by the agent's account
        remedy: remove the account's access to /var/log/journal (its group or an ACL): only the console should read it
  RED   /var/lib/docker is readable by the agent's account
        remedy: remove the account's access to /var/lib/docker (its group or an ACL): only the console should read it
  RED   cloud credentials file ~/.aws/credentials is present: the agent can use them to read logs at the provider
        remedy: keep cloud credentials out of the agent's account (another account, or short-lived credentials the agent cannot reach)
  RED   AWS metadata credentials answer (status 200): the agent can take the instance's cloud identity
        remedy: block the metadata service for the agent (a firewall rule, IMDSv2 with hop limit 1, no instance identity) or run it where it is not reachable

residuals (the console's own guards; warnings, whatever the profile):
  warn  Landlock is unavailable (ENOSYS): a docker source relies on the mounts alone
        remedy: a kernel with Landlock (5.13 or later, lsm=landlock), not disabled by the container runtime's seccomp profile
  warn  container shm-1 runs with IpcMode shareable: its /dev/shm mount can appear in the console's bound containers root
        remedy: use --ipc private (the default) unless another container joins it; Landlock guards the console against it
  warn  swarm mode is active: services' secrets are mounted under the containers root
        remedy: keep docker sources off a swarm node, or leave the swarm (docker swarm leave)

10 findings on production profile main: fix them, or run the agent in a container of its own (locklog setup --agent container)
